body:
The reject path described here looks already fixed on free5gc/smf main: since #236 (merged 2026-09-23), `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject` in `internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go` starts with `defer p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true)`, so the SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs are released even when building or sending the reject fails. The report was written against 2232d29 (v1.4.3), which predates that change.

What is still open on main is the accept side: `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` returns early on a build, token or N1N2MessageTransfer failure without releasing anything. There the PFCP session is already installed on the UPF, so whether to release locally, delete the PFCP session or leave it to the AMF looks like a decision for the maintainers.

Thanks @hsdfat for narrowing this down. I checked current main (1c9d766) and the accept side is still open: 

sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept in internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go returns early on four failures (building N1, building N2, the AMF access token, and N1N2MessageTransfer). Each leaves the SMContext in ActivePending, the UE IP and TEIDs allocated, and the PFCP session installed on the UPF. The AMF already received the 201, so nothing cleans these up.

I'd like to send a fix. It would follow the reject-side approach from #236: on failure, delete the PFCP session on the UPF, then call RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true) so the AMF is notified and the IP, TEIDs and PCF/UDM state are released. The local release still happens if the PFCP delete fails. TS 23.502 §4.3.2.2.1 describes this cleanup when establishment fails after the AMF has the context.

Does that match what the maintainers would want, or would you rather leave the release to the AMF?

Separately, I have SMF business metrics ready [https://github.com/free5gc/smf/pull/247]((https://github.com/free5gc/smf/pull/247) ) that make this kind of leak visible: establishment and release outcomes with their causes, current SM contexts per state, and PFCP request results and latency per UPF. They follow the AMF's internal/metrics/business pattern. A leak like this one shows up as a growing ActivePending count. I can send that as its own PR, and split it if that's easier to review.

Opened free5gc/smf#246 for the accept-side release. It defers a release in sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept that deletes the PFCP session and calls RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true) unless the session reaches Active, with tests for each failure path. Happy to adjust if you'd prefer a different approach.

@ae878

Thank you for reporting this issue.

Thanks @hsdfat for helping trace the code path and narrow down the problem, and thanks @maringantis for the detailed analysis and proposed fix.

We will review the issue and the proposed PR carefully, including the cleanup behavior and resource release flow after PDU Session Establishment failures.

We also appreciate the metrics proposal and will review it separately.
